claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic alloy with a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 lamellae have incoherent interfaces that create stress concentrations.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will cause a topological rearrangement of the lamellar structure.
The HPHT-induced rearrangement will convert incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent boundaries.
The treated alloy will develop a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will permit dislocation transfer between the two phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces will alleviate interfacial stress concentrations.
Stress alleviation at coherent interfaces will suppress interfacial cracking.
The coherent hierarchical structure will promote dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning.
The promoted deformation mechanisms will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
At high strain, the GND densities in the FCC and B2 phases will converge after HPHT treatment.
The treated sample will show elongated crack propagation rather than isolated microcracks.
The HPHT-induced structure will improve ductility without significantly reducing strength.
Coherent nanoscale internal interfaces can strengthen metallic materials.
Ordered B2 phases in high-entropy alloys are generally hard or strong and can increase yield strength through load transfer.
The pressure-temperature window must be high enough to generate the topological change but below the threshold for FCC/B2 phase decomposition or melting.
The specific conditions of 6 GPa and 1473 K satisfy the required FCC/B2 stability window.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments fail to produce the same hierarchical interface coherence or GND homogenization.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says coherent interfaces arrest or suppress interfacial cracking, whereas the predicted outcome calls for elongated crack propagation. Without explaining that elongated cracks are stable, deflected, or otherwise less damaging, crack arrest and enhanced crack propagation are in tension.
